claims: NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) is a super heavy-lift rocket.
NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) is an expendable rocket.
NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) is designed for deep space exploration.
NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) serves as the backbone for the Artemis program to return humans to the Moon.
SLS is the only rocket capable of sending the Orion capsule, astronauts, and cargo to the Moon in a single launch.
The purpose of SLS is to enable sustained human exploration of the Moon and future missions to Mars.
SLS generates 8.8 million pounds of thrust at launch.
SLS is the world's most powerful rocket.
SLS consists of a core stage with four RS-25 engines.
SLS consists of two five-segment solid rocket boosters.
Artemis I is the inaugural flight of SLS.
Artemis I successfully launched on Nov. 16, 2022.
Artemis II is the first crewed mission.
Artemis II is currently in preparation for a lunar flyby.
